specPoints.text: describe the stages in the production of cloned mammals involving the introduction of a diploid nucleus from a mature cell into an enucleated egg cell, illustrated by Dolly the sheep
understand how cloned transgenic animals can be used to produce human proteins

primer.text: Dolly the sheep proved a mature body cell could restart development. This note traces adult cell cloning from the enucleated egg cell through the electric shock that triggers division, to the surrogate mother that carries the embryo, and then shows how cloning amplifies transgenic animals that manufacture human proteins.

lessons.title: Adult Cell Cloning, Step by Step
lessons.opening: Adult cell cloning rebuilds an embryo from spare parts: an egg cell loses its nucleus, a diploid nucleus from a mature body cell takes its place, a small electric shock persuades the rebuilt cell to divide, and the growing embryo is placed inside a surrogate mother.
keyPoints: The nucleus is first removed from an unfertilised egg cell, leaving an enucleated egg cell.
A nucleus carrying the full chromosome complement (diploid) is taken from a mature body cell of the adult animal, such as a skin cell, and inserted into that enucleated egg cell.
A mild electric shock stimulates the reconstructed cell to divide by mitosis and form an embryo.
Embryo cells carry the same genetic information as the donated adult body cell.
At the ball-of-cells stage the embryo is inserted into the uterus of a surrogate mother, where it develops until birth.
Scottish scientists used this route in 1996 to create Dolly, the first clone of an adult mammal.

low.restatement: Empty an egg, drop in a skin-cell nucleus, zap it to start dividing, then park the embryo in a foster mother.
low.analogy: Swapping the hard drive of a computer with one loaded from an adult machine, then pressing the power button with a jolt.
low.examPointer: Recite the sequence with the key verbs — remove, insert, stimulate, insert again — and name Dolly as the exemplar for the final mark.

medium.restatement: An unfertilised egg cell loses its nucleus to give an enucleated egg cell; a diploid nucleus from a mature body cell takes its place; an electric shock triggers mitotic division into an embryo whose cells match the donor's genetic information; the ball of cells enters a surrogate mother's uterus and develops to birth.
medium.analogy: A handover in which the egg's original instructions are evicted and a full set from an adult tenant moves in, with electricity flicking the lights on.
medium.examPointer: Say diploid when describing the donated nucleus and enucleated for the emptied egg — the precise nouns carry the marks.

check.stem: What has been done to an egg cell to turn it into an enucleated egg cell?

options.text: Its own nucleus has been removed
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: Its cytoplasm has been replaced with agar
options.explanation: The cytoplasm stays; only the nucleus is taken out.

options.text: It has been fertilised by a sperm cell
options.explanation: The egg remains unfertilised throughout the procedure.

options.text: Its membrane has been stripped away
options.explanation: The cell membrane remains intact for the later insertion.

check.stem: From which cell is the diploid nucleus taken during adult cell cloning?

options.text: A mature body cell of the adult animal, such as a skin cell
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: A sperm cell from the same species
options.explanation: No sperm is involved; the nucleus comes from a body cell.

options.text: Another unfertilised egg cell
options.explanation: Egg cells supply the empty container, not the nucleus.

options.text: A bacterial plasmid
options.explanation: Plasmids belong to bacteria and are irrelevant to mammalian cloning.

check.stem: What does the small electric shock achieve in the cloning procedure?

options.text: It stimulates the reconstructed cell to divide and form an embryo
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: It fuses two egg cells together
options.explanation: Only one egg cell is involved at that stage.

options.text: It kills unwanted bacteria in the culture
options.explanation: Sterility is handled separately; the shock triggers division.

options.text: It wakes the surrogate mother's uterus
options.explanation: The shock acts on the reconstructed cell, not the surrogate.

check.stem: Where does the early embryo continue its development until birth?

options.text: In the uterus of a surrogate mother
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: In the Petri dish where it was created
options.explanation: The embryo leaves the laboratory for the surrogate's uterus.

options.text: Inside the sheep that donated the body cell
options.explanation: The donor provides only the nucleus, not the pregnancy.

options.text: In an artificial womb machine
options.explanation: No artificial womb features in the taught procedure.

check.stem: Why do the cells of the cloned embryo carry the same genetic information as the original adult?

options.text: Because the inserted diploid nucleus contains that adult's genome
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Because the egg cell adds matching DNA of its own
options.explanation: The egg's own nucleus was removed before insertion.

options.text: Because the electric shock copies the DNA
options.explanation: The shock starts division; it does not copy genetic material.

options.text: Because the surrogate mother contributes genes during pregnancy
options.explanation: The surrogate nourishes the embryo but adds no genes to it.

check.stem: State the role of the surrogate mother in adult cell cloning.
check.modelAnswer: The surrogate mother receives the early embryo in her uterus and carries it through development until birth.

check.stem: Name the first mammal cloned from an adult cell and the year that achievement was announced.
check.modelAnswer: Dolly the sheep, cloned in Scotland in 1996, was the first mammal produced by adult cell cloning.

check.stem: Explain why the plasmid-free egg cell must be enucleated before the donor nucleus is inserted.
check.modelAnswer: Removing the egg nucleus leaves the donor diploid nucleus in sole charge of development, so the clone expresses the adult body cell's genes rather than a mixture of two genomes.

check.stem: A farmer wants a flock of sheep all sharing one prize ram's genetics. Explain how adult cell cloning delivers this.
check.modelAnswer: Nuclei from body cells of the prize ram can each be inserted into enucleated eggs, shocked into embryos and carried by surrogates, so every lamb born carries the same prized genome.

lessons.title: Cloned Transgenic Animals as Protein Factories
lessons.opening: Once a transgenic animal exists, cloning multiplies it. A foreign gene coding for a useful protein is inserted into the animal's genome, the protein is harvested from milk, eggs or blood, and cloning builds a whole herd that manufactures the same medical product.
keyPoints: Scientists build a transgenic animal by adding a foreign gene to its genome.
The added gene may encode a useful protein, one the animal then secretes in its milk, eggs or blood.
Cloning a transgenic animal yields more animals carrying the same productive trait.
Transgenic animals supply useful proteins for medicine, including proteins that treat human diseases.

low.restatement: Give an animal a human gene, collect the protein it makes, then clone that animal to get a whole herd of tiny factories.
low.analogy: One goose laying golden eggs gets cloned until the whole flock lays golden eggs.
low.examPointer: For the protein question, name where the product appears — milk, eggs or blood — because examiners list all three routes.

medium.restatement: A foreign gene with medical value is added to an animal's genome so the animal secretes the human protein in milk, eggs or blood; cloning that transgenic founder produces a matched group of animals all expressing the same gene for large-scale protein harvest.
medium.analogy: A single brilliant chef writes the recipe into the kitchen itself, then the whole restaurant chain is cloned from that kitchen.
medium.examPointer: Link the two spec points when answering: cloning supplies the scale, transgenesis supplies the product.

options.text: A gene from another source has been inserted into its genome
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: It was born as an identical twin
options.explanation: Twins are clones, not transgenic organisms.

options.text: It has been fed a special protein diet
options.explanation: Diet changes the animal's meals, not its genes.

options.text: It was raised in a sterile laboratory
options.explanation: Where an animal lives says nothing about its DNA.

check.stem: In which products can a transgenic animal's useful protein be harvested?

options.text: Milk, eggs or blood
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: Sweat and tears only
options.explanation: Those fluids are not taught routes for protein harvest.

options.text: Urine exclusively
options.explanation: Urine is not part of the account.

options.text: Hide and wool
options.explanation: Skin fibres carry no secreted therapeutic protein.

check.stem: Why clone a transgenic animal once it has been created?

options.text: Cloning produces more animals that all express the same useful trait
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: To make the gene itself stronger
options.explanation: Cloning copies the genome; it does not upgrade the gene.

options.text: To remove the foreign gene from the line
options.explanation: Cloning preserves the inserted gene in every copy.

options.text: To let the animal recover before milking
options.explanation: Recovery is unrelated to cloning.

check.stem: Which medical use is intended for proteins from transgenic animals?

options.text: Treating human diseases with the harvested proteins
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: Flavouring everyday food products
options.explanation: The proteins are medicinal, not culinary.

options.text: Cleaning industrial equipment
options.explanation: No cleaning role is claimed for them.

options.text: Vaccinating the animals themselves
options.explanation: The goal is human therapy, not animal vaccination.

check.stem: Why does Dolly matter to the story of cloning mammals?

options.text: A nucleus from a mature adult cell can direct full development of a new mammal
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: That sheep milk is richer than cow milk
options.explanation: Milk composition was never the point.

options.text: That eggs can develop without any nucleus
options.explanation: Dolly's egg received a full diploid nucleus.

options.text: That cloning only works in laboratory insects
options.explanation: Dolly was a mammal, proving the method in large animals.

check.stem: State where a foreign gene is placed when producing a transgenic animal.
check.modelAnswer: The foreign gene is inserted into the genome of the animal, so its cells can express the new protein.

check.stem: Give one example of a human use for proteins harvested from transgenic animals.
check.modelAnswer: Proteins collected from transgenic animals can treat diseases in humans, supplying useful medicines.

check.stem: Explain why cloning amplifies the value of a successfully engineered transgenic animal.
check.modelAnswer: Creating the first transgenic animal is difficult, but cloning reproduces that exact genome repeatedly, so every clone secretes the same useful protein without redoing the engineering.

check.stem: A hospital needs a steady supply of a human blood protein. Design the production route using cloned transgenic animals.
check.modelAnswer: Insert the gene for that protein into an animal so it appears in milk, eggs or blood, then clone the animal so the herd supplies a constant, matching harvest for purification.

glossary.definition: An unfertilised egg cell whose own nucleus has been removed.
The adult female that receives the cloned embryo and carries it to birth.
A nucleus carrying the full two sets of chromosomes, taken here from a mature body cell.
An animal with a foreign gene inserted into its genome so it makes a useful protein.

figures.alt: Diagram showing cloning: cells from two sheep, with nucleus from sheep A inserted into egg from sheep B, after removal of original nucleus.
